cultural.vision_reason: This is a hand-drawn batik cloth with a classic parang (diagonal knife-wave) motif and floral border in indigo, brown/soga, and cream — a style historically associated with Javanese/Indonesian batik-producing regions, but batik of this kind (kain sarung) was also widely made and worn by Malay communities in Malaysia (e.g., batik blok/tulis traditions), so it is plausible as Malay dress textile.

physical.physical_description: Selendang (scarf) of cotton batik. Dark blue field, with repeating pattern of stylised rosettes in the spaces between a square trellis made up of further stylised rosette-forms. Patterns reserved in light brown or cream on the blue ground. Around the edges is a series of borders with scrolling floral and foliage designs in cream with touches of dark blue on a red ground.
